$comment: intent-match D19 backfill: shipped epics scored on the seed AS APPROVED (the seed in the commit that first added the epic README), with a PROXY ask (D8, C6 as corrected) and claims split by the builder. Answers live in each retro's _Intent:_ line, never here. Regenerate nothing by hand.

claims: The published SDK address moves to the new name.
The runtime provider identities and the live wire and data identifiers move to the new name.
The one public install exception under the old name is closed.
The mockup-only footnote ledger comes off the footer.
The signed-in product gets the mobile sweep the public routes already have.
A measured, written decision on whether and how to productize verification.
The cost and the findings of the verification pipeline are measured on the product's own code.
The pipeline is a frontier model writing specs, checkers checking them, and Jev triaging.
Nothing about verification is promised publicly before the verification module ships.
Every validated event is persisted exactly once.
Events are delivered asynchronously to configured destinations.
Product requests are never coupled to any vendor.
A failed delivery retries a bounded number of times and is visible as failed.
A failed delivery can be replayed by hand.
Miyagi's merchant-activation stream reaches its CRM view.
A PM can create a flag without typing JSON.
Targeting rules, variants and rollout are built visually.
A flag's history can be read without diffing JSON by eye.
The builder reaches the visual-targeting table stakes a direct competitor ships.
The final landing page is defined, per persona.
A launch-ready v1 stands up quickly from the already-shipped features.
A backfill contract makes every future epic light up its landing section.
An agent can create a kill-switch flag in every environment without a human.
There is an operating surface beyond the read-only, one-project MCP connector.
Consumers stop hand-rolling their own admin-API wrapper.
Signup provisions a working tenant instantly, with no hand provisioning.
Tenants have real human accounts.
Per-tenant isolation is hardened.
Credentials have a lifecycle.
The landing hero and pricing sections flip from waitlist to a real signup call to action in the same epic.
A sales artifact shows velocity, throughput, cycle and lead time, DORA and cost per shipped point.
It compares a human-baseline pod with an agent-augmented one.
It layers the outcome metrics the engine produces.
A live Roadmap Hub shows where we are against the desired end state.
The hub works at every grain: portfolio, epic and sprint.
It is beautiful enough to share with clients and investors.
It syncs from the docs that are already the source of truth.
A PM can build a simple A/B test without writing JSON.
Binding a flag is no longer a separate step limited to exactly matching variant keys.
The existing governance (immutable versions, SRM, interval, decision record) stays.
The console looks like the approved design.
The old UI is replaced, not hidden inside disclosures.
A test opens the approved design and compares the built pages against it.
Coverage is measured, never self-declared.
A North Star surface exists.
The Activity page is paginated.
The page says who the product is for now: a single maker operating a whole product.
The page names the four operating surfaces: product, delivery, security and resilience, and AI spend.
The page keeps its argument that decisions should carry receipts.
The console matches the approved design on screen, closing the five visible gaps.
An acceptance check can fail on the way a page looks.
The regenerator is committed and runs on a fresh clone.
The visual gate is not born with exemptions.
The design lives outside any one epic, so it does not expire when an epic closes.
Error and friction signals are captured into the engine.
Signals are grouped deterministically into structured tasks carrying product context (funnel position, flag state, experiment variant).
Tasks reach the customer's own agent over MCP, with read tools to pull them and staged write tools to claim and resolve them.
There is no integrated AI anywhere in the engine.
The landing's section 4 lights up in the same epic.
The signed-in product has a deliberate information architecture instead of a flat list of seventeen destinations.
A feature is the unit of work, with one page for it.
A feature's funnel and impact are reachable without typing a key into the URL.
Its switch, funnel, impact, experiment and history are related to each other in one place.
A PM who signs in sees what their agent did.
The agent window the landing promises appears inside the product.
Signing in lands on something better than a bare list of project slugs.
The feature areas are reachable and related to one another.
The methodology has its own place a reader can go: /methodology, with six chapters.
It teaches by doing.
Reading it feels like a different room from the sales page.
The method's second move is renamed from Shape to Design.
The landing's maker loop collapses from five steps to three: Consider, Operate, Exit.
The flags page is designed for a PM's job, not rendered from the engine's storage model.
A person can see which flags are on, and why others are not, on one screen.
The page stays usable at around 42 definitions.
Its words describe the job, not immutable versions, activations and snapshot revisions.
